output.population: 811 overweight adults assigned to four reduced-calorie diets for 2 years.
output.intervention: Four diets varying in targeted fat, protein, and carbohydrate percentages.
output.intervention_or_exposure: Reduced-calorie diets with different macronutrient compositions.
output.comparator: Factorial comparisons of lower versus higher fat, average versus higher protein, and highest versus lowest carbohydrate content.
output.outcome: Change in body weight at 2 years; satiety, attendance, lipid-related risk factors, and fasting insulin were also assessed.
output.effect: At 2 years, weight loss was similar for 15% versus 25% protein (3.0 vs 3.6 kg), 20% versus 40% fat (3.3 vs 3.3 kg), and 65% versus 35% carbohydrate (2.9 vs 3.4 kg); P>0.20 for all comparisons.
output.applicability_boundary: Applies to overweight adults receiving structured diet instruction over 2 years; the study tested reduced-calorie diets meeting cardiovascular-health guidelines rather than unrestricted versions of these macronutrient patterns.
output.source_span: By 2 years, weight loss remained similar in those who were assigned to a diet with 15% protein and those assigned to 25% protein.
